claims: KnowledgeChangeSet is the one immutable frontend-neutral domain-state change unit and binds exact contract, closure, prior state, ordered operation, temporal, supersession, dependency, and digest inputs.

One ordered semantic and protocol ledger is authoritative. One accepted temporal graph is derived by an identified projector replaying verified change sets, with no independent accepted-state write path.

Governed replay starts empty and receives its first domain records from a retained genesis change set or identified genesis set; current external-base runtime behavior remains an explicit implementation gap.
Proposal, checks, review, decision, and application cite the same change-set identity. ACCEPT may carry failure-atomic application without collapsing their distinct lifecycle records.

Foundation graph revision 23 and all Markdown projections contain the same 1,852 triples with zero set differences. All 395 status subjects have one status and the 109-node, 109-edge dependsOn graph is acyclic.
The strict 72-workstream DAG has 34 present cards and makes production KnowledgeGraph depend on the Small Shop KnowledgeChangeSet handoff. Population and operation plans remain derivation inputs.
Public guidance preserves optional lower profiles and labels persisted structural candidates non-governed and non-accepted until ledger admission.

The transaction adds design, documentation, canonical graph data, a zero-scope card, integration metadata, review rules, retained evidence, and tests only. It changes no runtime or ontology implementation.
limitations: No generic KnowledgeChangeSet runtime artifact, compiler lowering, public wire grammar, stable API, or alternate-language projector is implemented.
Current Python accepted-graph replay still consumes a caller-supplied GraphBaseArtifact rather than empty state plus retained genesis change sets.
Cross-contract ontology migration remains future work.
The self-inquisition rule is review-driven rather than a syntax-aware detector.

summary: Verify the single-ledger KnowledgeChangeSet architecture and dependency closure.
why: The retained report binds the exact decision, graph, semantic-history target, integration DAG, public boundaries, self-inquisition rule, and test bytes. Its checks establish one change-set unit, one ledger authority, replay-only accepted state, retained genesis, optional structural-only use, and zero runtime scope.
